title: Daily AI Digest: Mon, 26 Oct 2026
summary: A poisoned LiteLLM release shows how exposed AI tooling is, banks find unapproved agents in customer accounts, Anthropic says one agent often beats many subagents, outside auditors find gaps in OpenAI's agent monitoring, and Kimi K3.1 Pro shows cheaper tokens don't always mean cheaper tasks.

items.title: LiteLLM 1.107.0 was poisoned with a credential stealer
items.summary: LiteLLM sits in front of many enterprise LLM apps and holds every provider key, so it is a high-value target. Pin versions and image digests for AI tooling, keep gateway secrets in a vault, and treat model gateways like any other critical infrastructure.

items.title: Big US banks are finding AI agents inside customer accounts
items.summary: "Which agent is acting, for whom, and with what permission" is becoming the core enterprise question. Any agent you design that touches customer or operational systems needs its own identity, scoped and preferably read-only permissions, and an audit trail, never a borrowed human login.

items.title: Anthropic: one agent with on-demand context often beats a fleet of subagents
items.summary: This pushes back on "more agents is better" architectures. Start with one agent plus well-scoped skills, and add subagents only when evals show a clear need.

items.title: Outside auditors found gaps in how OpenAI monitors its own agents
items.summary: Monitoring is only as good as its coverage. When you design agent observability, check what slips through (long-running sessions, compressed context, actions that never return control) and test the monitor itself, not just the agent.

items.title: Kimi K3.1 Pro lands near the frontier, but cheaper tokens don't mean cheaper tasks
items.summary: Price per million tokens is the wrong number to compare models on. Measure cost per completed task on your own workloads. Also, a 2.8T-parameter model being "open" doesn't make it cheap to self-host; it needs serious GPU infrastructure.

items.title: Faster RAG documents: LlamaIndex's OCRia-1 now powers LlamaParse
items.summary: Messy PDFs and tables are where most enterprise RAG quality is lost. Better parsing upstream usually beats prompt tweaks downstream, and is worth testing on your own engineering and operations documents.

items.title: Framework heads-up: LangChain core 1.7 changes how tool-call arguments stream
items.summary: If you have a streaming UI that shows tool calls as they form, check it before upgrading. Otherwise these are safe maintenance upgrades.

items.title: Claude for Enterprise merges chat and Cowork, and Claude apps switch to auto mode
items.summary: If your department uses Claude Enterprise, admins have until 16 November to decide on the setting and update usage guidance. The broader lesson is that automated checks on each action are proving more reliable than humans clicking "Allow" all day.

title: Agent frameworks weekly roundup: 17–24 Oct 2026
summary: Security fixes and breaking changes in Pydantic AI, Microsoft Agent Framework, Google ADK, Mastra, the MCP TypeScript SDK and OpenAI Agents JS, plus memory, skills, eval and streaming updates from CrewAI, LangChain, LangGraph, Agno and the Claude Agent SDK.

items.title: Pydantic AI security advisories fixed in 2.58.0 and 2.59.0
items.summary: web_fetch could stall the process on hostile HTML, MCP config could leak server URLs and auth tokens into traces, and the Vercel AI / AG-UI adapters could run a tool with client-chosen arguments. Upgrade, then rotate any tokens that may sit in old traces.

items.title: Microsoft Agent Framework Python 1.23.0 breaking changes
items.summary: MCP 2.x migration, AG-UI endpoints now need an explicit authorization scope, and the Docker shell's extra_run_args is renamed unsafe_extra_run_args.

items.title: Google ADK 2.13.0 telemetry schema break
items.summary: Telemetry now defaults to the newer OpenTelemetry GenAI schema and drops the call_llm span, so dashboards built on it will go quiet. It also requires authlib 1.9.1+ for CVE fixes.

items.title: Mastra core 1.79.0 session, span and dependency breaks
items.summary: Agent sessions are keyed by sessionId, querySpans() lost its cost and model filters, and vulnerable dependencies were dropped.

items.title: MCP TypeScript SDK 2.4.0 stricter schema checks
items.summary: Stricter schema checks may reject some existing tools. Read the upgrade notes.

items.title: OpenAI Agents JS 0.21.0 removes the Runloop sandbox
items.summary: The Runloop sandbox provider was removed.

items.title: Google ADK 2.13.0 stable features and faster string-model agents
items.summary: 12 experimental features are now stable, MongoDB session and memory services arrived, and string-model agents run up to 8x faster.

items.title: MCP TypeScript SDK 2.4.0 adds Skills over MCP
items.summary: A server can publish a folder of reusable skills for clients to load.

items.title: CrewAI 1.15.29 eval export and memory-leak fix
items.summary: crewai eval can now run a crew and export the results. A fix stops private memories leaking into every recall.

items.title: LangChain core 1.7.0 tool-call-delta events
items.summary: Streamed tool-call arguments now arrive as tool-call-delta events. Update any custom stream parsers.

items.title: LangGraph thread priority settings
items.summary: The CLI and SDK gained thread priority settings.

items.title: Pydantic AI 2.61.0 citations and InputGuardrail fixes
items.summary: Structured citations across providers, plus InputGuardrail fixes.

items.title: Agno 3.1.x external agents and Sonnet 5.5 default
items.summary: AgentOS can run external ClaudeAgent and CodexAgent agents, and Claude() now defaults to Sonnet 5.5.

items.title: Claude Agent SDK 0.2.170 session history fix
items.summary: Parallel tool calls are no longer missing from session history.

items.title: Try ADK 2.13 MongoDbMemoryService
items.summary: Long-term memory through keyword recall, with no vector index or embedding model. An easy pilot for a department assistant that needs to remember past conversations without standing up a vector database.

title: Weekly AI Case-Study Deep-Dive: 23 Oct 2026
summary: Five pieces from SPE ATCE 2026 and Gartner: an evaluation harness for Occidental's drilling agent, a multi-agent rig scheduler (+16% projected production gain, -46% rig idle time), a physics-informed RAG agent for offshore gas networks (~90% faster notifications), ADNOC's AI digital twin (1-2% uplift, no extra capex), and Gartner's finding that only 13% of CIOs see significant AI value.

items.title: Building an Evaluation Harness for Oil & Gas AI Agents (Occidental, SPE ATCE 2026)
items.summary: Occidental's DrillingGPT eval (19 SME-curated tasks, each run 5 times) scored pass@5 of 63%, pass@1 of 48% and pass^5 of 37%. The agent can often reach the right answer, but not reliably.

items.title: A Multi-Agent AI Optimization System for Rig Utilization in the Burgan Field (SPE ATCE 2026)
items.summary: Cooperating agents around a genetic algorithm, with human approval kept throughout, projected a 90-day production gain of +16% and cut fleet-average rig idle time 46% versus manual schedules on identical inputs.

items.title: A Physics-Informed, Retrieval-Augmented Industrial Agent for Offshore Gas Networks (SPE ATCE 2026)
items.summary: A governed RAG agent with physical-consistency checks kept humans in operational authority. In eight matched event pairs, notification latency fell about 90% versus the conventional communication path.

items.title: AI-Enabled Digital Twins for Integrated Production Optimization (ADNOC AiPSO, SPE ATCE 2026)
items.summary: Phase 1 across eight producing fields in 2025-2026 gave a sustained 1-2% production uplift with no incremental capex. Autonomy is bounded by real-time engineering operating envelopes.

items.title: Gartner: Only 13% of CIOs Say AI Has Delivered Significant Value (19 Oct 2026)
items.summary: Only 13% of 2,002 CIOs report significant or transformational value. Organizations with rules for stopping pilots are 2.3x more likely to be vanguards, and with rules for retiring low-value production AI 2.6x, yet only 31% and 17% have them.

title: Daily AI Digest: Fri, 23 Oct 2026
summary: The agent stack is getting real infrastructure. Standards moved to a neutral foundation, clouds launched per-agent sandboxes, enterprises showed small fine-tuned models beating frontier ones on cost, and AI-found security bugs are now big enough to take sites offline.

items.title: AI found a critical PHP flaw (PHP2Shell) that puts WordPress, Drupal and Joomla at risk
items.summary: AI-driven bug discovery is speeding up disclosure cycles. The practical lesson is to patch, inventory which runtimes you actually run, and verify running builds. A WAF alone gives false confidence, and that applies to the internal tools your AI apps sit on too.

items.title: Palantir + NVIDIA: small fine-tuned Nemotron models beat frontier models on domain tasks
items.summary: This is the playbook for an industrial company like bp. Take a narrow, high-volume task with lots of labelled history, and a small local model can be cheaper, faster and easier to govern than a frontier API.

items.title: Agent Skills, Open Responses, OpenEnv and OpenSandbox join the Agentic AI Foundation
items.summary: The pieces you'd build an enterprise agent platform on (tools, skills, model APIs, sandboxes) now have vendor-neutral homes. That makes it safer to standardise on them internally. The proposed roadmap includes security guidance for writing and installing skills.

items.title: Microsoft Agent Framework (Python) 1.23 ships breaking MCP 2.x changes
items.summary: MCP 2.x migrations are starting to land in the major frameworks. Pin versions and test tool integrations before you upgrade, and note the secure-by-default push on endpoints and sandbox flags.

items.title: Every agent gets its own computer: Google's Agent Compute Engine, and Modal's sandbox boom
items.summary: Running untrusted agent code safely and cheaply is becoming its own infrastructure layer. Keep credentials outside the sandbox, give each agent its own identity, and stop paying for idle sessions. These are concrete design rules to borrow.

items.title: Nemotron 3.5 Bolt runs locally in about 24GB
items.summary: Capable open models that do tool calls and structured output now fit on a single workstation GPU. That makes private prototyping and on-prem pilots cheap to try before you commit to API spend.

items.summary: Evals are the skill that separates demos from production. This is a free, concrete framework you can bring back to your team.
